cues.en: Astrid mentioned that it's been a big part of my career working with NASA and the controlled environments of space. And we've flown stuff in the shuttle many times. And as this issue of vertical farming started to heat up, more and more and more magazine editors and journalists contacted me.
cues.zh: Astrid 提到，与 NASA 合作、研究太空的受控环境，是我职业生涯中很重要的一部分。我们多次用航天飞机把东西送上天。随着垂直农业这个话题开始升温，越来越多的杂志编辑和记者联系我。

cues.en: about, what do you think about this? Is this going to work? And what are their claims? And I started, there were so many, I had a canned response that I was sending them. Then this past summer, I was asked to speak at the annual meeting of the American Society for Horticultural Science on this topic. Now I gave a different talk there, but there's so many things to follow up on and refine that.
cues.zh: 问我怎么看这件事？这能行得通吗？他们的说法靠谱吗？一开始来问的人太多了，我就准备了一套固定回复发给他们。后来在刚过去的这个夏天，我被邀请在美国园艺科学学会年会上就这个主题演讲。我在那儿讲的是另一个题目，但有很多东西需要跟进和细化。

cues.en: great opportunity to do this again for this audience. Before I get into the details of this, I'm going to do a little sidebar. It's a three slide sidebar. And this is an article about 18 months ago in the New York Times, which I read every morning, get it online. This got forwarded around campus at the time widely. Nicholas Kristoff is a very widely known journalist for the Times.
cues.zh: 这次能再面向这群听众讲一遍，是个很好的机会。在进入细节之前，我先插一小段题外话，就三张幻灯片。这是大约 18 个月前 New York Times 上的一篇文章，我每天早上都在网上读它。当时这篇文章在校园里被广泛转发。Nicholas Kristoff 是 Times 一位非常知名的记者。

cues.en: And he said, professors, we need you. This is the headline of this story. Some of the smartest thinkers in the world are professors. I thought he was very gracious with saying we were smart. But his point, which I've emphasized here with this sculpture of Rodin's The Thinker, was that university scientists sit and pontificate and they don't get involved socially in the critical problems of the day.
cues.zh: 他说，教授们，我们需要你们。这是那篇报道的标题。世界上一些最聪明的思考者是教授。我觉得他说我们聪明，真是太客气了。但他的观点——我在这里用 Rodin 的《思想者》雕塑来强调——是大学科学家只会坐着高谈阔论，不参与解决当下关键的社会问题。

cues.en: We need you. You've got to get engaged. Of course, this generated a flurry of examples where professors are very engaged in social issues. But his point was, you need to be more engaged. Now let's fast forward 18 months to just a week ago. Another article in the New York Times.
cues.zh: 我们需要你。你必须参与进来。当然，这引发了一系列生动的例子，证明教授们非常关注社会议题。但他的观点是，你们需要更多地参与。现在让我们快进 18 个月，来到仅仅一周前。《纽约时报》上的另一篇文章。

cues.en: Food industry enlists academics in GMO lobbying war. This is academics lobbying Congress for legislation on GMOs. This is the first sentence of this article. Monsanto has brought in a rarefied group of advocates, academics, for the gloss of impartiality and the weight of authority that come with the professor's pedigree. And a little while later, people said professors have a white hat.
cues.zh: 食品行业拉拢学者加入转基因游说战。这是学者们在向国会游说关于转基因的立法。这是这篇文章的第一句。孟山都搬出了一群精英倡导者——学者，利用教授身份带来的中立光环和权威分量。不久之后，人们说教授头上顶着光环。

cues.en: And this article was not just about lobbying Congress in favor of GMOs, it was lobbying Congress also to ban GMOs. And again, there's academics on both sides of this. The two key people that were involved in this story are Charles Benbrook, who was right up the road at Washington State,
cues.zh: 这篇文章不仅涉及游说国会支持转基因，还涉及游说国会禁止转基因。同样，双方都有学者参与。这个故事中涉及的两个关键人物是查尔斯·本布鲁克（Charles Benbrook），他就住在离这不远的华盛顿州立大学，

cues.en: He is a research professor and as you know, that's not a tenure-track position. His position has been a hundred percent funded by the organic foods industry and he brings in a few hundred thousand dollars a year. He was terminated, not terminated, his contract was not renewed in May of this year before the New York Times story came out.
cues.zh: 他是一名研究教授，如你所知，这不是终身教职轨道。他的职位百分之百由有机食品行业资助，每年能带来几十万美元的资金。他在今年五月份、《纽约时报》报道出来之前被解雇了——也不是解雇，是合同没有续签。

cues.en: for mysterious reasons. They took off his web pages from the university, but he was involved in some very controversial research. I don't know what happened, but he's not with Washington State University anymore. On the other side, Kevin Foulter is a molecular biologist. He's the chair of the Horticultural Sciences Department in Florida. He has testified at Congress several times on GMOs about
cues.zh: 原因很神秘。他们撤下了他在大学网站上的网页，但他参与了一些极具争议的研究。我不知道发生了什么，但他已经不在华盛顿州立大学了。另一边，凯文·福尔塔（Kevin Folta）是一位分子生物学家。他是佛罗里达州园艺科学系的系主任。他曾在国会就转基因问题作证多次，关于

cues.en: He's testified on the safety of them. So the reason this is a big deal and the reason I got very interested is for one, Kevin Folta is a colleague. He publishes on photobiology. He's gracious enough to cite my papers when he publishes and I cite his papers. He's a top scientist. I really, really like him. So I opened my New York Times electronically and guess what I see?
cues.zh: 他曾就其安全性作证。所以这件事之所以是大事件，我之所以对此产生浓厚兴趣，首先是因为凯文·福尔塔是我的同行。他发表关于光生物学论文。他很慷慨，发表文章时会引用我的论文，我也会引用他的论文。他是一位顶尖科学家。我真的、真的很喜欢他。于是我打开电子版的《纽约时报》，你猜我看到了什么？

cues.en: because of a grammar request by the New York Times to the University of Florida, all of his emails on this topic, 174 pages. The moral of the story is, be careful what you say in email. It might end up on the front page of the New York Times. As I read through these, he didn't say anything I wouldn't have said. He was careful. He's never received any money, but
cues.zh: 因为《纽约时报》向佛罗里达大学提出了一项调取请求，他关于这个话题的所有邮件，共174页。这件事的教训是，发邮件时说话要小心。它可能登上《纽约时报》头版。我通读这些邮件时，他没说过任何我不会说的话。他很谨慎。他从未收过任何钱，但是

cues.en: Monsanto and other companies have paid his travel to Washington DC to testify. And that was bad enough. They said, oh, there you go. He's all tainted. He can't be impartial because they paid his travel. But he's never taken any money from them. And his department doesn't even get money from the biotech firms. So interesting sidebar about email and be ever vigilant about what you say in emails.
cues.zh: Monsanto 和其他公司支付他去华盛顿特区作证的差旅费。这就够糟了。他们说，哦，你看吧。他浑身是污点。他不可能公正，因为他们付了他的差旅费。但他从没拿过他们的钱。他的部门甚至不从生物技术公司拿钱。所以这个关于邮件的插曲很有意思，也要时刻警惕自己在邮件里说什么。

cues.en: End of sidebar. Back to vertical farming. Incredible claims have been made about what we're going to do with vertical farming. This is not a real photo. This is taken off the internet. It's a plan. If you go on the internet and type in vertical farming, hundreds and even thousands of images of incredible buildings are shown.
cues.zh: 题外话结束。回到垂直农业。关于我们打算用垂直农业做什么，有人提出了惊人的说法。这不是真实照片。这是从网上找来的。这是一张规划图。如果你上网输入垂直农业，会看到成百上千张惊人建筑的图片。

cues.en: I'm not going to show you very many of them, but I'll show you a couple of them. But let's look at the claims that people are making. These are people that are doing it or preparing to do it. Greensense Farms, one of the biggest. We use 0.1% of the water, land, and fertilizer of field farming.
cues.zh: 我不会给你们看很多，但会看几个。不过我们先看看人们提出的说法。这些是正在做或准备做这件事的人。Greensense Farms，其中最大的一家。我们的用水、用地和肥料用量只有田间农业的0.1%。

cues.en: Now, if that is true, field farming is toast. Everything is going to be in vertical farms. 0.1%. Zero carbon food. They're in London, and they're growing food in tunnels underneath London. Lower energy consumption than glasshouse growing. 70% less water. Again, if this is true, astonishing. Farm here is near Chicago.
cues.zh: 如果这是真的，传统农田种植就完蛋了。一切都将转向垂直农场。0.1%。零碳食物。他们在伦敦，在地下隧道里种食物。能耗比温室种植更低。用水少70%。再说一次，如果这是真的，那太惊人了。这个农场在芝加哥附近。

cues.en: Vertical farming greatly reduces our carbon footprint and minimizes the use of fresh water. So it's not hard to find a lot of claims. These are three of the big, big players in this. This is why I put them on here. And so I'd like to examine the validity of these claims in this talk. The book that ignited this is this one. Here's a copy of it, The Vertical Farm.
cues.zh: 垂直农业大幅减少我们的碳足迹，并最大限度减少淡水使用。所以不难找到很多说法。这是这个领域的三巨头。这就是我把它们放上来的原因。所以我想在这次演讲中检验这些说法的有效性。点燃这一切的书是这本。这里有一本，《垂直农场》。

cues.en: Desmond Despommier is a professor of public health at Columbia, and he started this maybe 10 years ago as a class assignment. What could you do in farms? His claims in this book, and he's probably been on 50 talk shows being interviewed about this because of the magic things that vertical farming
cues.zh: Desmond Despommier是哥伦比亚大学的公共卫生教授，他大概10年前把这作为一个课堂作业开始做。在农场里你能做什么？他在这本书里的说法，而且他可能上过50个脱口秀节目接受采访，因为垂直农业可能做到的

cues.en: might be able to do. He's been a huge proponent of this thing through this book and then there's multiple other books on this. But I want to make a little point here about the background of people and what happens when they get away from their core discipline. Note that he's a professor of public health. So now he's pontificating on agriculture
cues.zh: 神奇事情。通过这本书，他一直是这件事的巨大推动者，然后还有多本其他关于这个的书。但我想在这里稍微谈一下人们的背景，以及当他们偏离核心学科时会发生什么。注意他是公共卫生教授。所以现在他在对农业

cues.en: and the efficiency of agriculture. I want to show you a slide from one of my favorite scientists and one of my all-time favorite quotes on this topic. Werner Heisenberg, shown here next to talking to one of his buddies, an expert is someone who can avoid the worst errors in their own discipline. And we would like to train our graduate students. It's like the Hippocratic Oath. Do no harm. Don't screw it up.
cues.zh: 和农业效率高谈阔论。我想给你们看一张我最喜欢的科学家之一的幻灯片，以及这个话题上我一直最喜欢的一句引言。Werner Heisenberg，图中他正在和他的一位朋友交谈，专家是能避免自己学科中最严重错误的人。我们希望培养我们的研究生。这就像希波克拉底誓言。不伤害。别搞砸了。

cues.en: It's one thing to make a little progress, but don't screw it up. And I love that quote. An expert, someone that can avoid really bad errors in their own discipline because they understand it so well. You go to another discipline, you can make ridiculous assumptions pretty fast. Here's a diagram of what these look like. So, we're not going to go through this whole thing, but the key point on top of this, this whole thing, all these floors of
cues.zh: 取得一点进步是一回事，但别把它搞砸了。我非常喜欢这句话。专家就是那些在自己领域能避免重大错误的人，因为他们对其了如指掌。你换到另一个领域，很快就会做出荒谬的假设。这里有一个图表展示了这些东西的样子。所以，我们不会把整个内容都过一遍，但最核心的一点，在这上面，整个东西，所有这些楼层

cues.en: Plant growth here are going to be powered by one PV array and one vertical wind turbine and multiple layers of plants in this thing. There's a lot of other stuff in here which you can watch the video recording to see the details of this, but it uses all kinds of renewable technologies in this. It strikes me this is not unlike our building right here where we would like to think that those solar panels on the south side of this building power the whole building.
cues.zh: 这里的植物生长将由一个光伏阵列、一台垂直风力涡轮机以及这个装置中的多层植物来提供动力。这里面还有很多其他东西，你可以看视频录像来了解细节，但它在其中运用了各种可再生技术。这让我想起这就像我们现在这栋楼，我们总想当然地认为南侧的那些太阳能板能为整栋楼提供电力。

cues.en: And we have, we're a zero carbon building because we have a few solar panels out there. We've got a, here we go. Here's another diagram. This big tall skyscraper and some of the list of some of the crops. Now I know you can't see those names, so I'm going to blow this list of crops up. Here's some of the proposed crops for this. Let me circle them.
cues.zh: 而且我们，我们是一栋零碳建筑，因为我们在外面有几个太阳能板。我们有一个，好了。这里是另一个图表。这座高耸的摩天大楼以及部分农作物清单。我知道你看不清那些名字，所以我要把这个农作物清单放大。这里是为其提议的一些农作物。让我把它圈出来。

cues.en: Peaches, apples, cherries, we're going to grow trees in these, not just a few, not just some lettuce, trees. You talk to the apple growers in Washington State and tell them that they're going to be growing apple trees in skyscrapers, cheaper, and they can grow them in Washington State or cherries in Utah. This is not just proposed to
cues.zh: 桃子、苹果、樱桃，我们要在里面种树，不只是几棵，不只是长叶生菜，是树。你去跟华盛顿州的苹果种植户谈谈，告诉他们要在摩天大楼里种苹果树，成本更低，而且他们能在华盛顿州或者犹他州种樱桃。这不只是提议

cues.en: Grow a few fresh greens. This is all of our crops now. They don't have wheat on this list But in other articles they absolutely claim they're going to grow everything in here and field farming is going to become obsolete This isn't just far away. I learned recently that in Jackson Hole There's a company preparing this particular building for a vertical farm vacant lot
cues.zh: 只种几盘新鲜绿叶菜。现在这是我们所有的农作物了。这上面没有小麦，但在其他文章中，他们信誓旦旦地声称要在这里种植所有东西，大田耕作将变得过时。这不仅仅是很遥远的事。我最近了解到，在杰克逊霍尔有一家公司正在为这个特定的建筑筹备一个垂直农场，在一块空地上

cues.en: 100,000 pounds of produce. And this was just recently, February. Jackson Hole, the average income up there probably exceeds the sum of this whole room. They got enough money to put something like this in. So here's a little diagram of the history of agriculture in one picture. 100 years ago, we used animals, we used water coming out of the sky, and we produced Yale.
cues.zh: 产出 10 万磅农产品。这就在最近，二月份。杰克逊霍尔，那里的平均收入可能超过了这个房间里所有人的总和。他们有足够的钱来搞这种东西。所以这里有一张图，用一张图展示了农业的历史。100 年前，我们使用动物，利用从天而降的水，我们种出了产量。

cues.en: Very simple, very efficient. Now we fast forward to current agriculture and we've got big fossil fuel inputs, big irrigation inputs, both coming out of the ground, both in most cases in the long term, not sustainable. But now this same farmer, the size of that green arrow is roughly proportional to the size that that one farmer can produce.
cues.zh: 非常简单，非常高效。现在我们快进到现代农业，我们有大量的化石燃料投入、大量的灌溉投入，两者都来自地下，在大多数情况下长期来看都不可持续。但现在还是这位农民，那个绿色箭头的大小大致与那一位农民能生产的规模成正比。

cues.en: We're not outgrowing our own daily food anymore. We're using fossil fuels and groundwater to do it, and the groundwater spreads the area over which we can grow it. It took me a while to think about this slide, but I liked it because of the summary of where we've been going with agriculture. And many people say our current agriculture is just not sustainable, because those two arrows coming up from the bottom
cues.zh: 我们不再仅仅依靠自己每天的食物产出了。我们在用化石燃料和地下水来做到这一点，而地下水扩展了我们能种植的区域。我花了一段时间来思考这张幻灯片，但我喜欢它，因为它总结了农业的发展方向。很多人说我们当前的农业就是不可持续的，因为那两根从底部升起的箭头

cues.en: But here's the part of this slide that's the elephant in the room. There's one thing I hope that our students won't forget in terms of the energy input into any agricultural system. There is a massive amount of solar energy going into this, and I tried to scale the area under that yellow arrow to all the other arrows.
cues.zh: 但这张幻灯片最显而易见却鲜被提及的部分在这里。有一件事我希望我们的学生不会忘记，那就是任何农业系统中的能量投入。有大量的太阳能进入其中，我试图把那个黄色箭头下方的面积按比例对应到所有其他箭头。

cues.en: The energy from solar radiation to grow our food dwarfs all of these other inputs. We teach and we do models and calculate that crop productivity in the field is two to five percent efficient use of the energy in sunlight. So that green arrow is meant to be about two to five percent of the yellow arrow. So people say, oh yes, but we'll use solar panels for electricity to run these lights.
cues.zh: 太阳能辐射用于种植食物的能量，使所有这些其他投入相形见绌。我们教学并建立模型、进行计算，得出田间作物生产力对太阳光能量的利用效率为百分之二到五。所以那个绿色箭头本意是约为黄色箭头的百分之二到五。所以人们说，哦对，但我们会用太阳能板发电来运行这些灯。

cues.en: So I did the calculation, if we bought electricity off the grid, what would it cost for one season's worth of solar energy? If we're just going to buy electricity off the grid, run our most efficient lights, and we recently published a paper on the efficiency of electric lighting, using the best lights we have. This is LEDs and double-ended high-pressure sodiums now, which by the way are
cues.zh: 于是我算了一下：如果我们从电网买电，提供一个种植季所需的太阳能要花多少钱？假设我们只从电网买电，用最高效的灯。我们最近发表了一篇论文，研究电照明的效率，用的是目前最好的灯，包括 LED 和双端高压钠灯。顺带一提，它们现在的效率是八年前的两倍。

cues.en: twice as efficient as they were eight years ago. Electric lighting is getting a lot better fast, and it's not just LEDs, it's other technologies as well. If we had to pay the electric bill for that solar energy, $400,000 an acre. So if we're going to do urban farming and indoor farming under electric lights, we got to come up with a lot of money to pay the electric bill.
cues.zh: 电照明进步很快，不只是 LED，其他技术也在进步。如果要为这些太阳能支付电费，每英亩要花 40 万美元。所以，要是我们想在城市里种植，或在室内用电灯种植，就得筹很多钱来付电费。

cues.en: So, as I thought through this diagram, I'm thinking, okay, where does that electricity fundamentally come from? Right now it fundamentally comes from fossil fuels. So there's the diagram with indoor farming, same size of an arrow with...
cues.zh: 所以我看着这张图琢磨：这些电力从根本上说是从哪儿来的？目前，根本上还是来自化石燃料。这张图展示了室内种植，箭头大小相同，代表……

cues.en: fossil fuels coming out of the ground to run all those electric lights. It's an enormous cost. One of the things I told the reporter once, they kept bugging me about, don't you think this can work and we'll get better ways for electricity? And I said, look, it'll be fine. You can have a vertical farm if you let me have a vertical nuclear reactor right next to it to power it. And that helps get the point across for how much power it takes in these things. So let's look at what we could do
cues.zh: 从地下开采化石燃料，来驱动所有那些电灯。这成本高得惊人。有一次记者一直追问我：“你不觉得这行得通吗？以后我们会有更好的供电方式吧？”我说：“没问题。只要让我在垂直农场旁边建一座垂直核反应堆给它供电。”这样就能让人明白，这些东西需要多大的功率。接下来我们看看能用什么办法

cues.en: with solar photovoltaics. We can just use solar panels, right? And run the lights from those, and then there's no fossil fuels. Great. So this is a little model that any of you that have studied anything about radiation will understand. The visible light at solar noon is about 2,000 micromoles per meter squared per second. This is the photosynthetic photon flux
cues.zh: 利用太阳能光伏。我们可以直接用太阳能板，对吧？再用它们来给灯供电，这样就没有化石燃料了。很好。这是一个简单的模型，学过辐射相关知识的人都能看懂。太阳正午的可见光强度约为每平方米每秒 2,000 微摩尔。这就是驱动光合作用的光合光子通量

cues.en: that drives photosynthesis and plant growth. On the other side is the total solar radiation, 1,000 watts per meter squared, that would drive solar photovoltaics.
